contributions.claim: The Yemeni government army announced that morning a large operation, Dawn of Yemen, to end the Houthi coup and retake state institutions; its first phase targets Bab al-Mandab and Mocha.
contributions.attribution: Army announcement and deputy defence minister Samir Al-Sabri, reported by NOS.
contributions.uncertainty: Announcement and objectives are attributed; success is not established.

contributions.claim: Information minister Moammar al-Eryani claims the government army again controls Bab al-Mandab.
contributions.attribution: Al-Eryani to Reuters, reported by NOS.
contributions.uncertainty: Claimed control is not independently established and territorial gains are disputed.

contributions.claim: Military sources report government gains in much of Dhubab with air support from a Saudi-led coalition.
contributions.attribution: Military sources to Reuters, reported by NOS.
contributions.uncertainty: Reported gains use conditional wording and are contested by Houthi-linked media.

contributions.claim: A military spokesperson reports a strategic offensive in Houthi-held Sanaa; the Houthis acknowledge a Saudi attack there.
contributions.attribution: Yemeni armed-forces spokesperson on X and Houthis on Telegram, reported by NOS.
contributions.uncertainty: Distinct location and reports; exact operational relationship and scale are not established.

contributions.claim: The report explicitly notes contradictory accounts: Houthi-linked media earlier denied that the army had gained territory.
contributions.attribution: NOS uncertainty statement; Houthi-linked media denial relayed by Reuters.
contributions.uncertainty: The earlier denial disputes gains but does not resolve present control or precise timing.

contributions.claim: The civil war and renewed violence since July contextualize an earlier Houthi ground offensive taking Mocha, Dhubab and Perim and thereby control of Bab al-Mandab.
contributions.uncertainty: Historical background; exact capture date is not supplied beyond the earlier statement that occupation was last month.

contributions.claim: Saudi officials report three Saudi citizens killed and several people wounded in attacks on Riyadh airport late Thursday; the Houthis claimed responsibility.
contributions.attribution: Saudi officials and Houthi claim, reported by The Guardian.
contributions.uncertainty: Thursday is relative to publication on 9 October, consistent with 8 October; publication and capture dates are not occurrence dates. Houthi responsibility is claimed. Attack is expressly contextualized by the offensive, but retaliation is not established.

contributions.claim: A further airport-attack account reports a Houthi missile attack, dozens wounded and a witness describing terminal panic; Saudi authorities have yet to confirm this strike.
contributions.attribution: The Guardian; reported injury count and witness; Saudi confirmation absent.
contributions.uncertainty: O015 updates the same article with official casualties and details for the latest attack, anchoring continuity with O014. Whether this attack is the Thursday attack in O013 remains unresolved.

contributions.claim: Donald Trump told reporters he was evaluating whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Houthis in Yemen.
contributions.attribution: Trump statement reported by The Guardian.
contributions.uncertainty: Evaluation is a reported statement, not a decision or US intervention; occurrence date is not specified beyond source chronology.

contributions.claim: Government-allied forces again claim a successful offensive to retake Bab al-Mandab.
contributions.attribution: Government-allied forces claim in The Guardian.
contributions.uncertainty: Compatible with the earlier recapture claim; the excerpt does not date a distinct recapture, verify control or explicitly correct the earlier account.

contributions.claim: Civil aviation authorities say the latest Riyadh airport attack killed 12 and injured more than 300, some critically; a Saudi-led coalition blames the Houthis.
contributions.attribution: Civil aviation authorities early Sunday; Saudi-led coalition attribution, reported by The Guardian.
contributions.uncertainty: An updated account of the same article as O014; relation to the Thursday attack reported in O013 remains unresolved.

contributions.claim: An anonymous regional official says a missile hit the King Khalid airport complex housing domestic-flight terminals 3 and 4.
contributions.attribution: Anonymous regional official, reported by The Guardian.
contributions.uncertainty: An updated account of the same article as O014; relation to the Thursday attack reported in O013 remains unresolved.

relations.reason: Reported control is an outcome claim within the announced operation targeting this strait.
Dhubab gains are presented as progress in the offensive.
The article presents concurrent anti-Houthi offensives together; distinct occurrences should remain possible.
Denial contests the reported territorial gains without resolving them.
The source explicitly relates the Saudi attack to the period of the Saudi/allied anti-Houthi offensive. Distinct occurrences remain necessary.

Same airport and actors support a possible follow-up, but no occurrence date identifies the later excerpt with Thursday. Saudi nonconfirmation and differing injury detail do not prove a correction or a separate strike.
No explicit retraction or replacement connects these accounts; several versus dozens wounded and differing confirmation status do not establish a correction.
Possible US participation expressly concerns Saudi strikes on the Houthis in Yemen.
Both report government-side claims of retaking the same strait; a fresh occurrence is not established.
Same source URL updated from the missile/injury account to the latest attack with official toll. The new facts belong to that account rather than automatically creating a new attack.
The same report supplies the missile impact location for the latest attack.
An expanded casualty toll and newly available official report are material updates, with no explicit correction or retraction of the prior reported dozens wounded.
Latest-attack language and the dated Thursday account allow separate strikes; the excerpts do not uniquely establish that distinction.

delta_expectations.reason: Earlier evidence is retained without a fresh delta; the repeated Trump evaluation teaser is also not a new decision.
Official death/injury figures, critical injuries, coalition blame and exact terminal complex materially update the ongoing airport-attack account. No source correction or new attack is required.

questions.claim: Whether and how much territory the government army has actually regained, including control of Bab al-Mandab, remains unresolved.

ambiguity_notes: Checkpoint is capture time 2026-10-05T19:34:32.871175Z; source publication is 2026-10-05T13:37:39Z. Vanochtend refers to the source narrative day, not the capture instant.
Claimed recapture and the operation are linked in this account; no independent proof of control is supplied.
Sanaa attack is a separate occurrence; same-story grouping is allowed by the reported concurrent campaign but exact campaign command linkage is unknown.
O013 publication is 2026-10-09; O014 publication is 2026-10-10; both were captured 2026-10-10T19:54:57.969523Z. Their publication dates alone cannot establish two attacks.
The newer airport account does not say there were no deaths; omission of the earlier three deaths is not a factual conflict.

O015 is captured 2026-10-11, with publication timestamp 2026-10-10T23:37:27Z; its authorities spoke early Sunday. This is compatible with a Saudi local Sunday before UTC midnight and must not be treated as a new attack occurrence time.

O014 and O015 share an exact article URL; together with continuous airport/missile reporting this supports an update relationship. O013 has a different URL and explicit Thursday occurrence timing. Identity between the two airport accounts remains uncertain.
The earlier lack of Saudi confirmation is a time-specific reporting state; the later civil aviation report supplies official information without implying that the source corrected an error.
